PRICE PRIORS for recurring line types (statistical model fitted on the thresholds t revealed
in earlier games; gross amounts). How to use them:
- The amounts are final thresholds as they were revealed: they already contain whatever
  deductible, VAT and customary-price judgement applied in those cases, and they were computed
  from the full invoiced quantity (the whole quantity was indemnified there). For an
  indemnified line of this type take the stated amount for the line as t as it stands and give
  a price_log_sd that matches the stated range. Do not deduct a deductible from it and do not
  cut the invoiced quantity.
- Deviate only for something this case has and those cases did not: an aggregate cap or
  sub-limit that the lines of this invoice must share, a percentage reduction for a breached
  duty, or a purchase price or sum insured stated in the claim that limits the line.
- Whether a line is indemnified in THIS case is decided by the policy and the claim, not by
  the history. The history only says how often this line type was paid at all. A line type
  that was never indemnified before is usually an ancillary charge the policies do not carry;
  treat it as indemnified only if this policy clearly says so.

items.rationale: The failed indoor heating joint is consistent with covered non-frost fracture under §2.4.3(a). If all four elbows are documented as necessary for reconnection under §7.1.7(c), the gross allowance is €42.
Four elbows would be €42 if separately needed, but §7.1.8(c) and (e) exclude duplicate or unsupported quantities; the second set is not explained by the short repair.
Section 7.1.7(c) covers matching fittings, but §7.1.8(e) requires evidence that five 28 mm elbows were needed on this repair. If justified, the five-piece allowance is €104.
The five-piece allowance is €103 if documented, but §7.1.8(e) excludes quantities not attributable to the roughly one-metre joint repair.
One matching elbow would be €21 under §7.1.7(c) if its use in reconnecting the damaged section is established as required by §7.1.8(e).
Necessary fixings are covered under §7.1.7(c); the reference allowance for eight screws is €9.30.
Section 7.1.7(c) covers necessary clamps, but §7.1.8(e) requires the size to match the documented installation. Four clamps would be €19.20 if their use is substantiated.
Matching clamps for the billed 15 mm run qualify as fixings under §7.1.7(c); four at about €5.50 each total €22 if needed.
Section 7.1.7(g) covers customary repair labour. The reported site time supports this first 6.75-hour entry, calibrated at €619 gross.
The helper's attendance is confirmed, and necessary trade labour is covered under §7.1.7(g). The reference allowance for 5.75 hours is €409.
Section 7.1.7(c) covers like-for-like copper, but §7.1.8(e) excludes unsupported quantities. Only about one metre of the 6.4 m billed is supported, giving roughly €15.40 gross at the reference rate.
Section 7.1.7(f) allows the first travel charge from this contractor on the invoice; the reference allowance is €80.
Section 7.1.7(c) covers installation consumables used in the repair, provided they are not billed elsewhere under §7.1.8(c). The reference allowance is €43.
Section 7.1.8(b) expressly excludes contractor processing charges added to itemised labour and materials.
Section 7.1.7(c) covers like-for-like insulation, but §7.1.8(e) limits the quantity to the documented repair. About one metre of the six billed is supported, for €23 gross.
Sections 7.1.8(c) and (e) exclude duplicate or unsupported insulation; the claim does not establish a separate need beyond line 15. If all six mats were independently necessary, allow about €60.
Binding wire used to secure the replacement insulation is an installation consumable under §7.1.7(c); the reference allowance for two pieces is €26.
The reported day and a half broadly supports two distinct labour entries under §7.1.7(g), subject to no overlap under §7.1.8(c). The seven-hour reference allowance is €642.
Section 7.1.7(f) allows only one travel charge per contractor per invoice, even if the repair took more than one visit. A standalone charge would be €80.
Section 7.1.8(b) excludes the contractor's protective equipment. No separate covered repair consumable is identified in this bundled charge.
Sections 5.2.1 and 7.1.7(a) cover necessary disposal of removed pipe and insulation. The comparable gross allowance for this small load is €60.

Sections 7.1.5 and 7.1.8(a) and (e) exclude general cleaning and an unsupported coating. If necessary removal of leak residue can be separated from the bundled charge, allow about €100 for the local cleanup, not all five hours.
